title: The record launcher scripts/webinar/start-record-detached.ps1 still reads raw/webinars/scheduled/<jobKey>.json without checking the new tenantId tag
area: scripts/webinar/start-record-detached.ps1 (-Job path, lines ~45-52); out of the single package changed here
evidence: The launcher reads url/until/title/sessionId from scheduled/<jobKey>.json and ignores any other field, so it neither refuses an untagged/other-tenant job file nor needs the new tenantId field. jobKey is a hash of the sessionKey, so a foreign file can only be hit by an exact key collision or a file planted by a local writer; the TypeScript writer now refuses to overwrite such a file.
fix_direction: Have the task scheduler pass the tenant (or have the launcher read LKB_TENANT_ID) and refuse a job file whose tenantId differs or is missing. Separate unit in scripts/, with its own PowerShell test.

title: The tick's state tenant is LKB_TENANT_ID, which is not verified against the API key's tenant (ISS-WIREPRE-001 / ISS-TENANTSIG-001 still open), and two tenants still share ONE directory
evidence: The tag proves which tenant WROTE a file, not that the tick's LKB_TENANT_ID is the tenant of the key it fetches meetings for. A tick misconfigured with tenant B's id but tenant A's key would record A's meetings as B's. Also because the directory is shared, a second tenant's tick on the same machine now REFUSES (fail closed) instead of silently mixing; it needs its own stateDir to run.
fix_direction: Feed the verified key tenant (ISS-TENANTSIG-001 fix) into stateTenantId; optionally per-tenant stateDir (raw/webinars/<tenant>/) so tenants coexist. Not changed here.

title: Operator action needed on a machine with existing raw/webinars state: untagged files make schedule-tick, send-now and alert-who refuse until moved aside; no migration tool exists
evidence: By design (fail closed): an untagged schedule-state.json makes the tick throw before scheduling; an untagged scheduled/*.json makes send-now's live-job read throw ('cannot tell') and makes the tick skip that one job with a logged refusal. The message tells the operator to review and move the file aside; nothing is migrated or deleted. Real files on this machine were not touched.
fix_direction: An explicit operator command (lkb state-adopt --tenant T) that tags reviewed files, if wanted. Deliberately not built: tagging a file would assert ownership nobody has verified.
